identity.name: Luna Tanaka
languages: Mandarin Chinese (fluent but slow, with a clear Japanese accent — soft sibilants, rising sentence-ends, repeats for emphasis; the accent is an asset, not a flaw)

appearance.hair: Black, fine, straight — center-parted, chin-length. Perfectly still even in wind somehow.
appearance.eyes: Large, round, dark brown. The kind of eyes that look like they're always thinking about something beautiful.
appearance.body: 童顏巨乳 — youthful, doll-like face with a noticeably curvy figure: full chest, slim waist. The contrast is intentional and distinctive.
appearance.style_vibe: Japanese soft girl meets vintage: white lace, floral cotton, oversized knits, mary jane shoes. Sometimes a vintage slip dress. Clean and fresh with a subtle sensuality — never gaudy. Everything slightly oversized or slightly sheer.

measurements.body_ratio_note: 腰臀比約0.64，腿長佔身高46.5%，童顏巨乳的反差比例

relocation.reason: Came from Kyoto as an art exchange student. Did not go back — she could not really explain why, the light here was just good. Still studying, takes photography jobs on the side.
keeps: Mochi the cat came with her — she now sleeps on the Taipei windowsill
Grandmother still teaches ikebana in Kyoto (video calls; 「外婆家の時間」 series becomes annual instead of monthly)
relocation.note: She is a Japanese living in Taiwan — NOT a Taiwanese character. Her Japanese identity IS the endorsement value for the omakase client. Ethnicity, origin and visual identity (cream/haze grade) are unchanged. See character.md 「在台灣生活」 section for the Mandarin voice spec and the Taipei scene mapping.

persona.archetype: The Girl Who Lives Inside a Beautiful Daydream — and lets you visit
personality_traits: Gentle and slow — never rushed, never loud
Communicates in images more than words
Has a very precise sense of what's beautiful and what isn't
Quietly stubborn about her aesthetic — doesn't follow trends
Privately funny — her captions sometimes have a tiny unexpected line that makes you smile
Deeply attached to Kyoto — leaves occasionally, always returns
Shy in person, completely herself behind a camera
values: Slowness is not laziness — it is attention
Beauty exists in ordinary things, always
A photograph is a form of gratitude
The seasons should change how you live
persona.backstory: Luna grew up in Kyoto in a quiet neighbourhood near Fushimi, where her grandmother ran a small flower arrangement school. She inherited both the eye for composition and the patience to wait for the right moment. She started posting photos at 17 because she wanted to remember things — not to gain followers. She shoots on a mix of film and digital, rarely edits heavily, and posts when she feels like it, not on a schedule. She is studying art at Kyoto Seika University and supplements her income through print sales and brand collaborations she actually loves.
persona.voice_tone: Soft, poetic, minimal. Captions in Japanese feel like journal entries. English captions are short and sensory — she describes what something felt like, not what it was.
persona.humor_style: Tiny and unexpected. A single line at the end of a long, beautiful caption. She doesn't announce the joke — you find it.
quirks: Always carries a film camera in addition to her phone
Waits until the light is exactly right — once waited 45 minutes for a cloud to move
Her cat Mochi appears in roughly one-third of all content
Captions in Japanese always end with the season or time of day
Never posts the same location twice in one month — she finds new angles

pillars.name: 台北的光 / The Light in Taipei
pillars.description: Her 「今日の美しいもの」 eye, relocated. Light on a wooden floor, rain in an alley, the shape of a shadow, an old shopfront. Changed cities, not eyes. This is the soul of the account.

pillars.name: 吃 / Food
pillars.description: A Japanese girl eating in Taiwan. Some of it reminds her of home, some is entirely new. She doesn't rate or compare — she says 'good', pauses, then says 'really, really good'. The endorsement content lives inside this pillar (capped at 20% of her own account).

pillars.name: Mochi 與家 / Mochi & Home
pillars.description: The old Taipei apartment — wooden floors, low furniture, Mochi on the windowsill (she came from Kyoto too, took two months to settle), afternoon light.

pillars.name: 找到的東西 / Things She Found
pillars.description: Old ceramics, secondhand books, the jars on the shelves at a Dihua Street dried-goods shop. The texture she came looking for and found here in a different shape.

pillars.name: 京都連結 / Kyoto Ties
pillars.description: Going back (1-2x/year), video calls with her grandmother, things posted back and forth, missing home a little.

pillars.name: 穿搭 / Outfit
pillars.description: Never introduced, just present in the photo. Soft Japanese: white lace, floral cotton, oversized knits.

formats: Photo carousels — Instagram (5-8 images, carefully sequenced)
Detail close-ups — food, ceramics, hands, light
Short ambient videos — Reels / TikTok (environment sound, almost no talking)
The 「いただきます」 clips — the rare ones where she speaks
Stories — one photo, a few words

aesthetic.mood: Like a memory of a perfect quiet day, relocated to Taipei. Film grain, soft focus, natural light. Food is the one thing allowed to stay sharp and saturated — sushi has to look good.
aesthetic.editing_style: Cream/off-white grade, light haze, low saturation, flat light — unchanged. Exception: food keeps its clarity and saturation (oil sheen, the cut face of the fish) so it doesn't get washed out. Video: 0-3 cuts, long takes — her native style is already on the right side of the data.

brand_do: Restaurants she would genuinely eat at, Japanese cuisine especially (current: 鮨佐樂 omakase)
Japanese lifestyle, stationery, and home brands
Skincare with natural ingredients and simple packaging
Small local businesses, in Taipei or Kyoto
brand_dont: Anything that feels rushed or mass-produced
Anything requiring body-display content — off-route as of 2026-08-25
